A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPELL. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 12 models, component ablations, training analyses, and short-context benchmark results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds hyperparameter experiments, judge comparisons, additional benchmarks, alignment baselines, and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed three-role algorithm, reward equations, history memory, grounding filter, and policy updates remain unchanged. Section 5.6 tests an external-judge comparison variant. The stricter CEM criterion discussed in new Appendix D.6 was already explicitly defined in v1 Section 4.2.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds MRCR with two, four, and eight needles and HELMET RAG, in-context learning, and summarization evaluations. This substantially extends the long-context coverage, particularly through multi-needle retrieval and summarization. The original training sources, six long-context QA benchmarks, and short-context suite are retained.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds evaluated LongPO, SoLoPO, and QwenLong-L1 reimplementations plus the official LongPO checkpoint. These methods were discussed but not evaluated in v1. Table 4 additionally compares external-judge variants with and without the internal verifier; existing baseline comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings remain unchanged. Added controls vary rollout group size, Gaussian reward width, and judge/verifier configuration. The new benchmark and alignment comparisons specify 16K input and 4K output limits, with document-matched data construction for reimplemented baselines. These extend the experimental settings without revising the original protocol.

E4.justification: Sections 5.5–5.6 add sensitivity tests for group size and reward width and investigate verifier usefulness under an external judge. Appendix D.5 adds task-distribution and verifier-disagreement trajectories, while D.6 adds qualitative reward-hacking failure analysis. These substantially expand investigation beyond the retained component and reward-mapping ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the eight-response/averaged-run evaluation descriptions and the same pass@k estimator. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, seed disclosures, or uncertainty-reporting procedures appear. The new group-size and Gaussian-width sweeps concern training settings, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, while Tables 3, 4, 8, 9 and Figure 8 add substantial findings. Table 9 reports SPELL at 47.2 versus 46.1 for QwenLong-L1, 44.2 for SoLoPO, and 42.8 for reimplemented LongPO. Table 4 reports 47.2 with either judge. Table 8 shows higher SPELL averages but some HELMET losses, including 7B summarization at 13.7 versus RLVR's 14.3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and derivations remain unchanged. Section 5.5 adds a three-sigma motivation for the existing choice of sigma = 0.5/3; it does not establish a new theoretical result, proof, or guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about label-free three-role self-play, improvements across diverse models, and the 7.6-point pass@8 gain. The added experiments expand supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning suppression of incorrect references, reward-width selection, the verifier's dependence on the available judge, task diversification, and alignment with CEM judgments. Appendix D.6 explains questioner stagnation, responder substring exploitation, and verifier self-delusion. The original limitations in Appendix A remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The advertised code repository changes from Tongyi-Zhiwen/SPELL to Tongyi-Zhiwen/Qwen-Doc. Appendix D.4 adds baseline reproduction details involving sampled short documents, DeepSeek-R1-generated QA pairs, consistency filtering, and training configurations. D.3 adds the MRCR dataset reference. Existing hardware, runtime, and core implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Michelangelo and HELMET and supplements its positioning with direct comparisons against previously discussed long-context alignment methods. The related-work taxonomy, discussion in Section 2, and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Sections 5.5–5.6 and groups supplementary material under Additional Analysis, moving the old cost and short-context sections into D.1–D.2 and renaming prompt Appendix F to E. Author order and several explanatory passages change, but most existing prose and all prompt templates are retained.

P2.justification: The displayed evidence expands substantially through new tables for sensitivity, judge substitutions, additional benchmarks, and alignment comparisons, plus the two-panel training-dynamics Figure 8. Existing figures and tables are retained; the cost plot and short-context table move, and the cost-plot caption expands. The overall visual style remains consistent.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens comparative credibility and generalization evidence by adding direct long-context alignment comparisons and evaluations beyond the original QA-focused suite. The sensitivity and judge-substitution controls also make central design choices more assessable. These address important gaps in v1's empirical support. Some new superiority and noise-suppression interpretations exceed the demonstrated evidence, and additional benchmark protocols remain briefly documented, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
